---
title: "check-iterate-subscripts.yml"
---

Diff-scoped check that flags an iterate written with a subscript,
such as `\vcoef_t` or `\vcoef_{t+1}`.
The lab's notation rule writes an iteration index
in a parenthesized superscript,
as `\iterpoint{\vcoef}{\iter}`
(psw `chapters/notation/delimiters-and-scripts.qmd`, from
[psw#543](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/psw/issues/543)).
The check keeps the mismatch from coming back after a notes repository
converts its existing pages
([lds#2435](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/lds/issues/2435)).

The check flags a configured symbol followed by `_` and an iteration index
on a line a pull request adds,
in `.qmd`, `.Rmd` and `.md` files.
The index is bare (`\vcoef_t`) or braced (`\vcoef_{t}`, `\vcoef_{t-1}`,
`\vcoef_{\iter+1}`).
Each finding reports the file, the line,
and the suggestion `\vcoef_{t+1} -> \iterpoint{\vcoef}{t+1}`.

## Symbols and indices

The `symbols` input names the macros whose subscripted use is an iterate,
without the backslash (default `vcoef steplen`).
The `indices` input names the index letters or macros (default `t \iter`).
An index is one of them with an optional `+` or `-` and a number.

The check does not flag:

- an index that is a number alone, such as `\vcoef_0`,
  because a true parameter has that name;
- an index letter not in `indices`, such as `\vcoef_k` by default,
  because `k` often names a coordinate;
  add `k` to `indices` where a page uses it for an iteration;
- a symbol not in `symbols`;
- the conforming `\iterpoint{\vcoef}{\iter}`;
- a code fence or code span, an HTML comment, or YAML front matter;
- a line carrying, or following, `<!-- check-iterate-subscripts: allow -->`.

## Scope

Only lines a pull request adds are reported,
so existing pages never block,
and a page converts when someone edits it.
An added line whose exact text was also deleted in the same diff
counts as moved rather than new.

With no `base-ref`, or when the diff cannot be computed
(a shallow clone, an unresolvable ref),
the check skips with a warning.
It never falls back to a whole-tree scan.
Set `whole-tree: true` to scan every tracked file in full on purpose,
for example to count the subscripted iterates a repository still carries.

Every run prints how many lines and files it examined.

## Limitations

- A use split across lines
  (the symbol at the end of one line, `_t` at the start of the next)
  is not found.
- A brand new untracked file is invisible to `git diff`.
  Stage it to have a local run examine it.

## Inputs

| Input            | Type    | Default | Description |
| ---------------- | ------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `symbols`        | string  | `'vcoef steplen'` | Space- or comma-separated macro names, without the backslash, whose subscripted use is an iterate. |
| `indices`        | string  | `'t \iter'` | Space- or comma-separated iteration-index letters or macros. Add `k` where a page uses it for an iteration and not for a coordinate. |
| `globs`          | string  | `'*.qmd *.Rmd *.md'` | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive by default). |
| `paths-ignore`   | string  | `''`    | Comma- or newline-separated glob patterns (relative paths) to skip. Supports `*`, `?` and recursive `**`. |
| `fail`           | boolean | `true`  | Fail the workflow when a subscripted iterate is found. Set `false` to warn only. |
| `whole-tree`     | boolean | `false` | Scan every tracked file in full instead of only a PR's added lines. |
| `python-version` | string  | `'3.x'` | Python version to set up. |
| `runs-on` | string | empty (`CI_RUNNER` variable, else `ubuntu-latest`) | Runner label for the job. Use a self-hosted label only for a private repository; never for a public one, whose pull requests can run arbitrary code on it ([#1167](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1167)). |

## Permissions

Only `contents: read` (the default), so no `permissions:` block is needed.

## Example

```yaml
# Copy to .github/workflows/check-iterate-subscripts.yml in your repo.
# Diff-scoped check: flags an iterate written with a subscript, such as
# `\vcoef_t` or `\vcoef_{t+1}`, on lines a PR adds, and suggests
# `\iterpoint{\vcoef}{\iter}` (an iteration index in a parenthesized superscript).
# Blocks by default; existing pages never block, since only added lines count.
# Only contents:read is needed (the default), so no permissions block is required.
name: Check iterates written with a subscript

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-iterate-subscripts.yml@v3
    # with:
    #   symbols: 'vcoef steplen'                # macro names whose subscripted use is an iterate
    #   indices: 't \iter'                      # index letters or macros; add k where it is an iteration
    #   globs: '*.qmd *.md'                     # pathspecs to check (recursive)
    #   paths-ignore: 'chapters/outtakes/**'    # skip known-noisy paths
    #   fail: false                             # warn instead of block (defaults to true)
    #   whole-tree: true                        # scan every line, not just a PR's additions
    #   runs-on: private-runner                # self-hosted runner label (private repositories only)
```

See
[`examples/check-iterate-subscripts.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-iterate-subscripts.yml)
for the full caller stub.
